I really wanted to like Charlie Murder. The art style is cool, the music slaps, the beat-em-up gameplay has a lot of personality, and the band-themed chaos is genuinely fun in short bursts. It’s clear there’s a good game here at its core.
Unfortunately, I cannot recommend it.
The balancing is highly questionable, especially in single player. The lack of proper invincibility frames after getting hit is brutal — you’ll get stun-locked constantly by groups of enemies, taking chip damage while you’re helplessly flailing. It turns fights that should feel satisfying into pure frustration.
There are also some obvious bugs that hurt the experience. The camera is frequently unhelpful, especially in tighter areas or during big enemy swarms, often leaving you unable to see what’s hitting you. But the worst offender is a game-breaking bug: a very difficult optional boss did not drop a necessary item required for the good ending. I looked it up and confirmed it was a known issue for some players.
I actually managed to finish the game completely solo. Yes, it’s possible. But it was one of the most unenjoyable and frustrating experiences I’ve had in a while. What should have been a fun, over-the-top brawler turned into a tedious, rage-inducing slog.
This game could probably be a blast with friends — the co-op chaos would likely cover up a lot of the jank. But playing alone? It’s a huge hassle and extremely difficult in the worst way possible. Not the rewarding kind of hard, just poorly designed and punishing for no good reason.
Verdict: Skip it unless you have friends to play with and don’t mind carrying the team through some serious flaws.

It's like if you put Sid Vicious in charge of developing Streets of Rage.

That is to say, it RULES.

Now, for the long-winded review.

I grew up in the 2000's. It was a darker time, thematically. Creepypastas were all the rage, blood and guts were a must, and Ska-punk ruled the world. Or, at least, that's how it felt being exposed to Newgrounds animations and early YouTube.  It was brutality and darkness for the sake of it, but it almost had a certain innocence to it. It was done not just for the sake of provocation, but for the sake of "this is the coolest thing we can think of."

Charlie Murder is a perfect time-capsule of those days. Bloody, dark, and over the top, but earnest. The use of Flash animation, the grittiness of every environment, and of course, the music, everything just screams "HELL YEAH!"

The gameplay can be a tad janky, but it doesn't need to be perfect. It just needs to be fun. Where else can you get magic powers from a sleazy tattoo parlor? Where else do you get a beat-'em-up with rhythm sections and trashing a hotel room? Where else is there a beer-crafting mechanic to give you stat boosts? I'll save you the trouble - Nowhere else.

Charlie Murder is one of a kind. And I love it. I love it to death.
